turns.speaker: practitioner
turns.text: Hi, it's Aven. Last time you mentioned wanting to cut back on soda. How has that been sitting with you this week?

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: Honestly, I've thought about it a lot. I'm drinking like four cans a day, and I feel kind of gross after.

turns.speaker: practitioner
turns.text: Four cans a day is leaving you feeling worse, not better.

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: Yeah. And my dad has diabetes, so it's always in the back of my mind.

turns.speaker: practitioner
turns.text: Seeing what your dad goes through makes your own health feel close to home. What matters most to you about staying healthy?

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: Being around for my kids. I want to be able to keep up with them.

turns.speaker: practitioner
turns.text: Keeping up with your kids is what this is really about for you.

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: It is. I don't want them growing up thinking soda with every meal is normal.

turns.speaker: practitioner
turns.text: You want to show them something different.

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: Right. And I know I can do it. I went a whole month without soda last spring.

turns.speaker: practitioner
turns.text: You've already proven to yourself that you can go without it.

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: Yeah, until work got crazy and the vending machine was right there.

turns.speaker: practitioner
turns.text: Let me pull this together. Soda is leaving you feeling gross, your dad's diabetes keeps your health on your mind, and you want to keep up with your kids. You've done this before, and stress at work is what pulled you back. Did I get that right?

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: Yeah, that's it exactly.

turns.speaker: practitioner
turns.text: You've got a clear picture of why this matters, and it sounds like you're ready to think about a first step.

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: Maybe I could swap the afternoon can for sparkling water. That's the one I grab out of habit.

turns.speaker: practitioner
turns.text: The afternoon can is more habit than craving, so that's a smart place to start.

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: I could keep a few cans of sparkling water in my desk drawer.

turns.speaker: practitioner
turns.text: Having it within reach takes the vending machine out of the picture. What else would help on the stressful days?

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: Maybe just reminding myself why I'm doing it. For my kids.

turns.speaker: practitioner
turns.text: Keeping your kids in mind is your anchor on the hard days. On a scale from zero to ten, you're about an eight in confidence, so let's lock that in.

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: Sure, an eight sounds about right.

turns.speaker: practitioner
turns.text: Swapping the afternoon can is a plan built around your day. It's your plan, and you can change it any time. When would you like to check in on how it's going?

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: Next Tuesday works.
